confusions: The debt answer on the borrowing-cost page says the UK is 'lower than Japan, Italy, the United States, France and Canada and higher than Germany', which reads oddly and I had to work out that it meant second lowest.
The IMF and OECD debt measures were both shown with a switch and I could not tell which one the question meant, so I did not trust either for the comparison.
On the Work section I only found the overall 16 to 64 employment rate, not the age-group figures for 18 to 24 and 25 to 34 year olds, so I could not answer those questions and stopped looking.
The UK interest-payments figure was described as 'the third highest of the G7' and I had to check the chart to see which countries were above it.
The 2008-09 home-ownership figure was not stated in words, so I read it roughly off the chart and I am not sure of it.
The Back button sent me to an earlier page rather than back to the section I came from, which cost me actions.
Scrolling a long page on the phone was slow, so I ran out of my 40 actions before reaching the defence, welfare, debt-history, manifesto and OBR sections, and I left those as Not sure.
The 'Who pays' section mixes HMRC and ONS figures, and the 46.0% figure and the 36.2% figure were close enough that I had to read the label carefully to see what each measured.
